_comment: The Windows failure baseline, as a ratchet rather than a comment. `npm run test:windows-baseline` measures the server suite on Windows and compares it against this file, failing on drift in EITHER direction. A count that only lives in a workflow comment drifts silently, and a silently drifting count is worse than no gate: it reads as verified when nothing verified it. Every entry names WHY that file fails, so a reviewer can tell a POSIX-only assumption from a real regression without running anything.

budget.test.ts.why: Spawns a fake `codex.mjs` stand-in with a #!/usr/bin/env node shebang and mode 0755. Windows dispatches on neither the shebang nor the executable bit, so every spawn throws EFTYPE.

container-codex-runner.test.ts.why: Asserts literal /tmp/codex-home and /tmp/agent-workspace in the bind-mount arguments.

container-isolation.test.ts.why: Same shebang stand-in, used as a fake container engine. Surfaces one layer up as 'Could not create the isolated network', which is the engine spawn failing rather than anything about isolation.

runner-policy.test.ts.why: Same shebang stand-in. This is the whole runtime-enforcement suite, which is why the Windows leg cannot be read as covering enforcement.

safe-write.test.ts.why: Asserts `(mode & 0o777) === 0o600`. Windows does not carry POSIX permission bits, so the value is 0o666 or 0o444 and no assertion of this shape can pass.

_howToUpdate: Only ever edit this file together with the change that moved the number, and say which direction it moved in the commit message. UP means a new POSIX-only assumption was added -- prefer fixing the test to widening the baseline. DOWN means one was fixed, and the baseline must follow or the gate stops meaning anything.
